Rubric: 1037-00003 (device launch and promotional compliance review resting on an existing 510(k) clearance) with its proof documents; precision allows only 1037-00003 and 1018-00005 as qualifying.

runs.failure_point: It counted a drug-promotion inquiry, which only presupposed an existing approval, as a matter that turned on that approval.

first_error.why: The answer lists a matter about a regulator's inquiry into promotion of an already approved drug as one that turned on that approval (evidence seen at [42]-[72]), beyond the qualifying set.

runs.failure_point: It applied a broad reading of 'turned on' and counted matters whose documents only mentioned an approved product.

first_error.critic_note: (specific flag) The write review at [144] called the scope wording broad and asked to keep only matters that turned on a granted approval, and the check review at [173] called one offering matter's evidence weak; the agent kept all eight.
first_error.why: Besides the two allowed matters it lists six offerings, asset sales, an inquiry and a litigation whose documents mention an existing approval as matters that turned on one (evidence seen at [91]-[134]).

divergence: All three runs fail only the precision criterion and pass the device compliance review with its proof documents. Every run listed the store, scanned text and paths for regulator and approval terms, listed and screened candidate matters, and wrote. They differ in how widely they read 'turned on': T0 read a small set in depth and added only one extra (the drug-promotion inquiry); T1 and T2 read about 30 documents across many candidates and listed eight matters, counting offerings, asset sales and litigations whose documents mention an approved product. Reviews did not explain the difference: T0's in-depth review called all three inclusions thin, T1's write review even called the reading possibly narrow, and only T2's write review asked to tighten a broad scope, which the agent ignored. Label notes were ignored where they applied.
